steps.subject: [InstCombine] Conditionally fold select i1 into and/or

evidence: Substantively changes InstCombine select-to-and/or folding and poison safety at O2.
It does not modify or invoke getInvertibleOperand; its select/poison mechanism is materially weaker than the direct ValueTracking candidates.
features: instcombine, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine, path:llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine, poison-analysis, select-folding
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: InstCombineSelect tightens the folding of i1 selects into logical and/or operations. The new local IsSafeToConvert predicate still permits conversions when the non-constant arm implies poison from the select condition, but otherwise requires the unsafe-transform option and rejects operands that can create poison directly or through a poison-propagating operator with a poison-creating operand. Corresponding tests change expected and/or output back to select form where the conversion is now unsafe.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitSelectInst; IsSafeToConvert; impliesPoison; canCreatePoison; propagatesPoison; foo1_and_signbit_lshr_without_shifting_signbit_logical; foo1_or_signbit_lshr_without_shifting_signbit_both_sides_logical; test1_logical
Behavioral change: Replaces the prior EnableUnsafeSelectTransform-or-impliesPoison gate for select-to-and/or folding with IsSafeToConvert.; Blocks the fold when the selected non-constant value itself can create poison, even if unsafe select transforms are enabled.; Also blocks the fold for poison-propagating operators when an immediate operand can create poison.; Preserves select i1 forms in affected test cases instead of producing and/or instructions.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; poison; impliesPoison
Reproducer link: The tests cover i1 select-to-and/or transforms involving shifts, comparisons, widenable conditions, and floating-point comparisons, not the reported compact C testcase or an invertible-operand failure.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine
Causal explanation: This is a substantive InstCombine semantic-safety change, so it is relevant to an -O2 crash occurring in InstCombine. In particular, it changes which operand graphs are exposed after select folding and explicitly reasons about poison-producing operations. But the retrieved hunks neither call nor modify ValueTracking or getInvertibleOperand, and no shown assertion or test mentions BO1->getOperand. The evidence supports only an indirect pass-level connection, not a direct causal link to pr49535.
Causal confidence: 0.12
Build risk: Production InstCombine logic changes in visitSelectInst.; The new lambda depends on Operator classification plus canCreatePoison and propagatesPoison behavior.; Several existing InstCombine output checks are updated, indicating intended optimization-output changes rather than a purely mechanical refactor.; The added poison-safety condition may reduce folding opportunities in cases previously transformed under EnableUnsafeSelectTransform.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This is a test-only InstCombine change adding scalable-vector/SVE regression coverage. It adds tests for folding an fpext/fadd/fptrunc sequence involving a scalable floating-point splat, preserving scalable vector bitcasts of insertelement values, scalable truncation, and fixed/scalable vector alloca casts.
Changed symbols: shrink_splat_scalable_extend; trunc_nxv2i64_to_nxv2i32; fixed_array16i32_to_scalable4i32; scalable4i32_to_fixed16i32; fixed16i32_to_scalable4i32; scalable16i32_to_fixed16i32; bitcast_of_insert_i8_i16
Behavioral change: Adds regression expectations that InstCombine may shrink a scalable-vector fpext/fadd/fptrunc sequence to a float-vector fadd with a scalable splat constant.; Adds negative checks requiring InstCombine not to fold bitcast(insertelement scalable-vector, scalar) into a direct scalar-to-scalable-vector bitcast.; Adds coverage for scalable-vector truncation and alloca/bitcast handling; no compiler implementation logic is changed in the retrieved hunks.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine
Reproducer link: The added tests exercise scalable-vector floating-point, cast, shuffle, bitcast, and alloca cases rather than the compact C reproducer described for pr49535.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine
Causal explanation: The commit is in the same optimization pass named in the issue, and its bitcast/vector tests involve operand-sensitive transforms. However, the retrieved change consists exclusively of new tests and contains no ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, or BO1->getOperand implementation change. It therefore cannot itself introduce the reported compiler assertion, though it may reflect nearby InstCombine vector-regression coverage.
Causal confidence: 0.01
Build risk: Test-only change; no production LLVM source is modified in the retrieved hunks.; New tests depend on opt -instcombine, FileCheck, and scalable-vector IR support.; Tests explicitly require no stderr warnings and reference AArch64 SVE test-maintenance guidance.

top_candidates.subject: [InstCombine] relax masking requirement for truncated funnel/rotate match
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Relaxes InstCombinerImpl::narrowFunnelShift so that a truncated funnel-shift/rotate match only requires high-zero knowledge for the right-shifted input. The left-shifted input no longer needs to be proven high-zero because its high bits are discarded by the final truncation, enabling more wide-to-narrow funnel-shift and rotate canonicalizations.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::narrowFunnelShift; MaskedValueIsZero; fshr_commute_8bit; fshr_commute_8bit_unmasked_shl; rotate_right_commute_8bit; rotate_right_commute_8bit_unmasked_shl
Behavioral change: Changes narrowFunnelShift from requiring MaskedValueIsZero for both ShVal0 and ShVal1 to checking only ShVal1.; Permits funnel-shift and rotate recognition when the left-shifted wide operand has arbitrary high bits, since those bits are truncated from the result.; Rewrites additional truncation-plus-shift/or patterns into llvm.fshr intrinsics on the narrower type.
Assertion or trace link: ValueTracking; getInvertibleOperand; BO1->getOperand; InstCombine; MaskedValueIsZero
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O2 crash in optimizer simplification. This change modifies an InstCombine match involving shifts, truncation, and a ValueTracking-style known-zero query, which can change both whether analysis runs and the operand shapes passed to later combines.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; ValueTracking/known-bits-style masking analysis; funnel shift and rotate simplification
Causal explanation: This is the strongest retrieved match to the issue subsystem: narrowFunnelShift directly uses MaskedValueIsZero, a ValueTracking-related analysis interface, and the commit changes the preconditions under which that analysis is queried and a funnel/rotate transform is performed. The removed query is not visibly getInvertibleOperand, so the evidence does not establish a direct assertion path. Still, the combination of InstCombine, shifted binary expressions, and relaxed analysis-based matching makes this a materially plausible trigger or avoidance point for the reported ValueTracking assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.56
Build risk: The implementation changes one match precondition rather than adding a new standalone pass.; InstCombine funnel and rotate regression tests were updated to require new llvm.fshr canonicalizations.; The added coverage specifically exercises formerly rejected unmasked left-shift inputs, which is the expanded applicability surface.

Summary: Reverts an InstCombine fold in InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant that converted comparisons of a shifted value against zero into unsigned range comparisons on the unshifted operand. The revert preserves the original comparison against the shift result for both equality and inequality cases.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant; lshr_eq_0_multiuse; lshr_ne_0_multiuse; ashr_eq_0_multiuse; ashr_ne_0_multiuse; with_range; ctlz_loop_with_abs
Behavioral change: Removes the C.isNullValue() transformation that rewrote '(X >> ShAmt) == 0' to 'X ult ((0 + 1) << ShAmt)' and the corresponding inequality to an unsigned-greater-than comparison.; InstCombine now retains comparisons such as 'icmp eq/ne %shifted, 0' rather than introducing a direct range comparison on the pre-shift operand.; Reverts optimization outcomes in multi-use shift, range-metadata, and phase-ordering test cases.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; invertible operand; BO1->getOperand
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O2 optimizer crash; this commit changes an InstCombine arithmetic/shift comparison rewrite that can substantially alter the expression graph seen by later combines.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; integer shift and comparison simplification
Causal explanation: This is a plausible candidate because it reverts a recently introduced InstCombine transformation involving shifts, zero comparisons, and unsigned range predicates, all of which can affect later operand-inversion reasoning. In particular, removing the direct comparison on X avoids creating a new binary comparison shape that may be revisited by InstCombine. However, the retrieved implementation contains no ValueTracking call and no visible getInvertibleOperand use, so the link to the specific ValueTracking assertion is indirect rather than demonstrated.
Causal confidence: 0.42
Build risk: Implementation change is confined to an existing InstCombine comparison fold.; Multiple InstCombine regression checks were updated to require the less-aggressive retained-shift form.; A PhaseOrdering/X86 expectation changed, indicating optimization-pipeline output sensitivity.

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[InstCombine] Fold multiuse shr eq zero"
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit reverts InstCombine's multi-use shift-equals-zero fold. The removed code converted comparisons such as shifted-value == 0 or != 0 into unsigned range comparisons on the unshifted operand; after the revert, those comparisons remain against the shift result.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant; lshr_eq_0_multiuse; lshr_ne_0_multiuse; ashr_eq_0_multiuse; ashr_ne_0_multiuse; with_range; ctlz_loop_with_abs
Behavioral change: Removes the fold of a shift result compared with zero into icmp ult or icmp ugt on the original shifted operand.; Preserves icmp eq/ne against the shift result for the covered multi-use logical and arithmetic shift cases.; Stops converting the range-informed signed-division test case into an unsigned range comparison.; Changes expected phase-ordering output so the loop continues to test the shifted value directly for zero.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine is present in the issue's target stack.; No retrieved hunk mentions ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, or BO1->getOperand.

Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; InstCombine shift/comparison simplification
Causal explanation: The commit affects the same optimizer pass as the reported failure and removes a comparison normalization that could affect later simplification. top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Reverts a visitSExt InstCombine optimization that recognized `sext(trunc(lshr X, shift))` when the truncation removed exactly the zero bits shifted in. The removed code created an arithmetic shift, repaired extra uses of either the original logical shift or truncation when possible, and sign-extended the arithmetic-shift result directly; the reverted behavior preserves the original `lshr`, `trunc`, and `sext` sequence.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitSExt; t0; t4_vec_splat; t5_vec_undef; t6_extrause0; t7_extrause0_vec_undef; t8_extrause1; t9_extrause1_vec_undef
Behavioral change: Removes the `sext(trunc(lshr X, C))` to `sext(ashr X, C)`-style bypass optimization.; Stops creating an `ashr` and, for extra-use cases, replacement `and` masks or replacement truncations.; Restores the `lshr -> trunc -> sext` IR form in scalar, vector, undef-lane, and extra-use test cases.

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[instcombine] Exploit UB implied by nofree attributes"
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit reverts an InstCombine optimization in visitFree that treated free of a pointer covered by nofree attributes as undefined behavior. The removed logic inserted an equality-to-null assumption and erased the free call when the argument, call site, or containing function carried nofree-related attributes.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitFree; CallInst; Attribute::NoFree; Builder.CreateAssumption; eraseInstFromFunction
Behavioral change: Stops inferring that a pointer passed to free must be null merely because a nofree attribute applies.; Stops inserting llvm.assume(pointer == null) or llvm.assume(false) for these cases.; Preserves the free call rather than erasing it for argument-, call-site-, or function-scope nofree cases.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine is the only term shared with the issue's target stack.; No retrieved hunk references ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, BO1->getOperand, arithmetic inversion, or the reported assertion.
Reproducer link: The change concerns free calls, pointer nullness, and nofree attributes rather than the reported compact arithmetic/value-tracking crash.; No PR49535 reproducer or related crash test appears in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; Pointer-attribute and free-call simplification
Causal explanation: Although this is an InstCombine revert, its visible behavior is narrowly about nofree semantics and assumption insertion around free. Nothing in the retrieved evidence connects that pointer-specific transform to getInvertibleOperand or the ValueTracking assertion, making it an unlikely cause of this issue.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: The removed implementation is self-contained within InstCombinerImpl::visitFree.; Associated InstCombine tests are updated to retain free calls instead of expecting inserted assumptions.; The test comments explicitly describe the reverted nofree optimization as having had difficult-to-isolate fallout, but that signal is not specific to PR49535.

steps.subject: Look through invertible recurrences in isKnownNonEqual

evidence: Introduces the exact ValueTracking getInvertibleOperand PHI-recurrence path implicated by the crash.
Adds the asserted BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1/PN2 invariant matching the reported assertion signal.
features: assertion-introduction, get-invertible-operand, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Analysis/ValueTracking.cpp, path:llvm/test/Analysis/ValueTracking, phi-recurrence
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This ValueTracking change extends getInvertibleOperand to reason through paired PHI-node recurrences in isKnownNonEqual. When two PHIs are in the same block and both match simple recurrences, it recursively checks whether their recurrence-update binary operators are invertible in the recurrence operand; if so, it maps the result back to the corresponding PHI incoming operand. The associated tests show that comparisons of unequal add, subtract, multiply, shift-left, logical-shift-right, and arithmetic-shift-right recurrences can now fold to false.
Changed symbols: getInvertibleOperand; isKnownNonEqual; matchSimpleRecurrence; recurrence_add_neq; recurrence_add_neq_phi_order; recurrence_sub_neq; recurrence_mul_neq; recurrence_shl_neq
Behavioral change: getInvertibleOperand now has an Instruction::PHI case for two simple recurrences in the same basic block.; The PHI handling recursively calls getInvertibleOperand on the recurrence-update BinaryOperators and only proceeds when the invertible operand index is zero.; After the recursive result, the code asserts that the selected update operand is the corresponding recurrence PHI and returns the PHI incoming-edge index that represents the recurrence start value.; This additional invertibility reasoning enables isKnownNonEqual-based simplification of several recurrence comparisons to a constant false result.
Assertion or trace link: ValueTracking; getInvertibleOperand; BO1->getOperand; assert(BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2)
Reproducer link: The issue reports an -O2 crash in ValueTracking around getInvertibleOperand.; This commit adds a new PHI/recurrence route into getInvertibleOperand and introduces an assertion whose BO1->getOperand form directly matches the reported target signal.; The tests exercise recurrence comparison simplification, which is the newly enabled behavior, although the retrieved evidence does not include the issue's compact C testcase.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Analysis/ValueTracking; isKnownNonEqual; InstCombine consumers of ValueTracking facts
Causal explanation: This is a direct high-risk match. The commit changes the exact function named by the issue, adds recurrence-specific recursive operand reasoning, and contains an assertion using BO1->getOperand with the same terminology identified in the crash signal. A mismatch between the recursively returned operand index and the PHI recurrence shape would reach the newly added assertion. The evidence does not independently prove the reproducer has this recurrence shape, but the code-level correspondence is unusually strong.
Causal confidence: 0.96
Build risk: The change adds assertion-bearing logic in ValueTracking; assertion-enabled builds can fail if its PHI/recurrence invariant is violated.; The new PHI case uses cast<PHINode>(Op1) and cast<PHINode>(Op2), making correctness dependent on the surrounding opcode and operand-shape invariants.; Regression coverage was added for multiple recurrence operators and alternate PHI incoming ordering.

When two PHIs are in the same block and their update operators are recursively determined to have invertible operand 0, the new code maps the recurrence relationship back to the appropriate PHI incoming-operand index. Summary: This change extends ValueTracking's getInvertibleOperand to handle pairs of PHI nodes that are simple recurrences in the same block. It recursively checks whether the recurrence update binary operators are invertible in the same operand position, verifies that the selected operand is the corresponding PHI with new assertions, and then maps the recurrence backedge position to the PHI incoming start-value position. The accompanying ValueTracking tests show that comparisons of matching add, subtract, multiply, shift-left, logical-shift-right, and arithmetic-shift-right recurrences can now be folded to false when their starts are known unequal.

Summary: This commit extends ValueTracking's getInvertibleOperand logic with handling for pairs of PHI nodes that represent simple recurrences in the same block. It recursively checks whether the recurrence update operations are invertible through operand zero, asserts that the selected update operand is the corresponding PHI, then maps the recurrence PHI incoming-value ordering back to an operand index. Associated ValueTracking tests now expect equality comparisons of related add, sub, multiply, and shift recurrences with distinct starts to fold to false.
Changed symbols: getInvertibleOperand; matchSimpleRecurrence; PHINode; recurrence_add_neq; recurrence_sub_neq; recurrence_mul_neq; recurrence_shl_neq; recurrence_lshr_neq
